==Problem==

NASA’s Perseverance Rover was launched on July <imath>30,</imath> <imath>2020.</imath> After traveling <imath>292{,}526{,}838</imath> miles, it landed on Mars in Jezero Crater about <imath>6.5</imath> months later. Which of the following is closest to the Rover’s average interplanetary speed in miles per hour?

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 6{,}000 \qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 12{,}000 \qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 60{,}000 \qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 120{,}000 \qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 600{,}000</imath>

==Solution 1==
Note that <imath>6.5</imath> months is approximately <imath>6.5\cdot30\cdot24</imath> hours. Therefore, the speed (in miles per hour) is <cmath>\frac{292{,}526{,}838}{6.5\cdot30\cdot24} \approx \frac{300{,}000{,}000}{6.5\cdot30\cdot24} = \frac{10{,}000{,}000}{6.5\cdot24} \approx \frac{10{,}000{,}000}{6.4\cdot25} = \frac{10{,}000{,}000}{160} = 62500 \approx \boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 60{,}000}.</cmath>
As the answer choices are far apart from each other, we can ensure that the approximation is correct.

~apex304, SohumUttamchandani, MRENTHUSIASM

==Solution 2.1==
Note that <imath>292{,}526{,}838 \approx 300{,}000{,}000</imath> miles. We also know that <imath>6.5</imath> months is approximately <imath>6.5\cdot30\cdot24</imath> hours. Now, we can calculate the speed in miles per hour, which we find is about
<cmath>\dfrac{300{,}000{,}000}{6.5\cdot30\cdot24}=\dfrac{10{,}000{,}000}{6.5\cdot24}=\dfrac{10{,}000{,}000}{13\cdot12}=\dfrac{10{,}000{,}000}{156}\approx\dfrac{10{,}000{,}000}{150}\approx\dfrac{200{,}000}{3}\approx\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 60{,}000}.</cmath>
~MathFun1000

==Solution 3==

The rover traveled about <imath>292{,}526{,}838 \approx 300{,}000{,}000</imath> miles. <imath>6.5</imath> months is about <imath>6\cdot 30 + 15 = 180 + 15 = 195 \approx 200</imath> days. <imath>200</imath> days is about <imath>200\cdot 24 \approx 200\cdot 25 = 5{,}000</imath> hours. <imath>\frac{300{,}000{,}000}{5{,}000} = \boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 60{,}000}</imath>

==Remark==
This problem is a great example of a situation where rounding all the numbers to ones we can easily work with is an excellent first step. In any competitive timed test, especially the AMC, if you see problems that require you to choose answers that are the closest, this is a sign to you that you can speed through this problem and move on quickly. 
The rounding being: <imath>\frac{30000000}{200*20}</imath>
~Nivaar
